title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (from the previous page): S_0 is smooth over a perfect field k, S is a formally smooth formal lift over W(k), and F_S is a Frobenius lift compatible with σ. C is the category of tuples (P', Q', M, ∇, F_M, Fil). Here P' and Q' are twisted-constant p-adic lattices (étale Z_p-local systems). M is an extension 0→Q'⊗O_S→M→P'⊗O_S→0. ∇ is an integrable connection respecting the extension, with the canonical connections on the graded pieces. F_M: F_S^*M→M respects the extension and induces F_{Q'} (the canonical iso) on the sub and pF_{P'} on the quotient. Fil is a splitting of the reduction M_0 compatible with F_{M_0}. Grothendieck asks whether the Dieudonné functor from ordinary Barsotti–Tate groups on S_0 to C is an anti-equivalence.

This page begins '1) Description de la catégorie C' by making C explicit through cocycle data.
(1) Choose an O_S-splitting φ: M ≅ P'⊗O_S ⊕ Q'⊗O_S. Any other splitting φ' differs by a unipotent automorphism u(x,y) = (x, y+Lx), with L ∈ Γ(T⊗O_S) and T = P'^∨⊗Q' = Hom(P',Q').
(2) Transport F_M through F_S^*(φ) and φ, using the canonical identifications F_{P'}, F_{Q'} (the struck/half-legible 'I_{P'}, I_{Q'}'). One gets F_{M,φ}(x,y) = (px, y+Φx), with Φ = Φ_{M,φ} ∈ Γ(T⊗O_S).
(3) Change of splitting: F_{M,φ'}∘F_S^*(u) = u∘F_{M,φ} gives Φ' + F_S^*(L) = Φ + pL, i.e. Φ' = Φ + (pL − F_S^*L).
(4) Marginal note: one may choose φ compatible with Fil on S_0. Then the admissible L vanish on S_0, and Φ does too.

The next page completes this. The connection form ω ∈ Ω^1⊗T changes by ω' = ω − dL, and the object conditions are dω = 0, F_S^*ω − pω = dΦ, Φ_0 = 0.

So C (with fixed P', Q') is the groupoid of 1-cocycles of the two-term-to-three-term complex T⊗[O_S → (O_S ⊕ Ω^1) → (Ω^1 ⊕ Ω^2)]. The differentials are L ↦ (pL − F^*L, −dL) and (Φ,ω) ↦ (F^*ω − pω − dΦ, dω), i.e. the mapping cone of (p − F^*) on the de Rham complex, with a mod-p condition from Fil.

This is exactly the shape of the syntomic/'crystalline Kummer' complex computing Z_p(1)-cohomology. A multiplicative Serre–Tate parameter q ∈ T⊗(1+mÔ) gives L = log q, ω = dlog q, Φ = log(q^p/F^*q). The purpose is to reduce the equivalence question for ordinary BT groups to comparing this H^1 with Ext^1(étale, multiplicative) = Kummer/Serre–Tate data on S_0.
errors: The boxed formula places Φ in Γ(Ť⊗O_S), but Φ must be a section of T⊗O_S = Hom(P',Q')⊗O_S. The next page uses T for ω and the transformation law Φ' = Φ + pL − F^*L forces Φ and L into the same sheaf; the check over Ť is presumably a slip or overwrite.

Matrix conventions are mixed. The direct sum is written P'⊕Q' with u(x,y) = (x, y+Lx), but u and F_{M,φ} are written as upper-triangular matrices (id L; 0 id) and (id Φ; 0 p·id). These are correct only in the ordering (Q', P'). The formulas u(x,y) and F(x,y) = (px, y+Φx) are the consistent ones.
F_S^*(L) tacitly means the σ-semilinear pullback combined with the canonical Frobenius identifications of the twisted-constant P', Q'. This is fine but implicit.
The derivation Φ' + F_S^*L = Φ + pL is correct.

ideas.what: Description of an ordinary F-crystal (extension of a unit-root by a slope-1 unit-root twist) with connection by cocycle data (Φ, ω) modulo coboundaries (pL − F^*L, −dL)
ideas.modern_name: Extensions of F-crystals / the cone of (p − F^*) on the de Rham complex; syntomic complex for Z_p(1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dwork (Frobenius structures); Katz (Travaux de Dwork 1972; Serre–Tate local moduli 1981); Deligne–Illusie (Cristaux ordinaires et coordonnées canoniques, 1981); syntomic formalism: Fontaine–Messing 1987, Kato

ideas.what: Change-of-splitting law Φ' = Φ + pL − F_S^*(L)
Question whether the Dieudonné functor from ordinary BT groups on S_0 to crystal data with Frobenius lift and Fil is an equivalence
ideas.modern_name: Crystalline Dieudonné theory over smooth bases (ordinary case); Serre–Tate canonical coordinates
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (ICM 1970 problem), Messing, Berthelot–Breen–Messing, de Jong (1995), Katz/Deligne–Illusie for ordinary
ideas.where_published: Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux (ICM Nice 1970); Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné (Montréal 1974) pose the general full-faithfulness question

missed.claim: Around 1970 Grothendieck already models ordinary Dieudonné crystals with Frobenius lift as cocycles of what is essentially the mapping cone of (p − F^*) on the de Rham complex. This is the syntomic-type complex whose H^1 is the crystalline Kummer group of units. It anticipates the structure later exploited by Katz and Deligne–Illusie (canonical coordinates) and by Fontaine–Messing (syntomic Z_p(1)).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority only: the computation itself is standard now. It shows Grothendieck's own route to the ordinary case of the Dieudonné equivalence, via explicit cohomological reduction to Kummer theory, predating the published treatments.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, correct, early explicit cocycle description of ordinary Dieudonné crystals. It foreshadows the Dwork/Katz/Deligne–Illusie canonical-coordinate picture and the syntomic complex, but the mathematics itself is now standard, so the interest is mainly historical.

'[-En termes de-] et I_{φ'}, I_{Q'}' is more plausibly '[-En termes de-] et I_{P'}, I_{Q'}', i.e. the canonical identifications F_{P'}, F_{Q'} used along with φ and F_S^*(φ).
F_{M,φ}(x,y) = (px, y+Φx) is legible in the image (no [?] needed).
